messages.subject: Cross validation
parts:
Hi all -

I have been using the 'occu' fitting function and would like to perform model validation.  Due to the smallish sample size (n=75) I would like to use a K-fold method instead of partitioning my data into training and validation sets.
However, the cross validation functions I have attempted to use (cv.lm, CVbinary, CVlm) are designed to work with S3 class objects, not the S4 class which unmarked uses.  The as(obj,"S3") function does not work.

I have attempted to modify the cv.lm function but I'm not sure how to handle the multiple site visits that occu allows for in the model definition that cv.lm uses.  Has anyone found a cross validation function that handles S4 classes?

Thanks for your help

Patrick

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Cross validation
parts:
Hi Patrick,

Here is a leave-one-site-out cross-validation example that I had laying around. Use with caution! There are no safety checks and this will give you misleading results if you compare models fitted to data with different numbers of missing values. Note also that there are many other, possibly better, ways of doing this type of thing.

Richard

library(unmarked)
set.seed(33140)
example(unmarked) # Fits 3 occupancy models fm1,fm2,fm3
# Discrepancy measures
cost.fn1 <- function(observed, expected) mean(abs(observed-expected)>0.5)
cost.fn2 <- function(observed, expected) sum((observed-expected)^2)

xval <- function(fm, cost) {
    umf <- getData(fm)
    nSites <- numSites(umf)
    cv <- 0
    for(i in 1:nSites) {
        test <- umf[i,] # leave one site out
        train <- umf[-i,]
        fmu <- update(fm, data=train)
        E.psi <- predict(fmu, type="state", newdata=test)[,1]
        E.p <- predict(fmu, type="det", newdata=test)[,1]
        E <- E.psi * E.p
        y <- as.vector(getY(test))
        cv <- cv + cost(y, E)
    }
    return(cv)
}

xval(fm1, cost=cost.fn2)
xval(fm2, cost=cost.fn2)
xval(fm3, cost=cost.fn2) # Lowest error

Perhaps I should not have posted this function because it is not very general and could easily be misused. However, my guess is that you just need to remove missing values in the cost function:

cost.fn2 <- function(observed, expected) sum((observed-expected)^2, na.rm=TRUE)

Richard
